newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean future ends up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean future ends up in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up in slow trade on Monday on short-covering, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,150 yuan ($380) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 3,150 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,160 and a low of 3,142 yuan per tonne.
November rose 10 to 3,170, the January 1998 contract 13 to 3,148 and March eight to 3,148 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 20,300 tonnes from 23,800 tonnes.
Soybeans opened little changed and short-covering pushed prices up for most of the session, raders said.
"Short-covering from retail investors was responsible for today's gains," one trader said.
"Other active futures markets such as copper attracted the attention of many investors," he said.
Traders said they expected retail investors to continue moving their money out of the soybean market, a fact which would lead soybeans to consolidate in a narrow range in the short term.
